subject: DPA: clarification on incident obligations, deliverables, and escalation path
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@greenfieldpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@greenfieldpay.com
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA discussion - incident obligations

Jordan,

Thanks for the walkthrough today. Two quick asks from our side before legal signs off on the DPA:

1) Can you confirm the maximum notification window you can commit to for incidents that may affect personal data? Our counsel is pushing for 24 hours for "material breaches" and 72 hours for anything else; we want to understand what Redwood can realistically meet given your forensic processes.

2) If a customer requests a snapshot for their forensic review, what are the constraints on scope (full tenant export vs scoped logs) and who pays for transfer/escrow?

I've attached the redlines we're proposing so you can reference the exact clauses.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our onboarding timeline is tight.

Best,
Liam
Director, Security & Compliance
Greenfield Payments

Attachment: DPA_redlines_v3.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@greenfieldpay.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA discussion - incident obligations

Liam — thanks, and great questions. High level answers below; forwarding to legal ops for exact wording and to ops for runbook specifics.

- Notification windows: our standard commitment in the DPA is "as soon as reasonably practicable" with an internal target of 48 hours for incidents that meet our "exposure of personal data" threshold. We can discuss a 24-hour SLA for material incidents on a case-by-case basis (requires an SLA addendum and additional support pricing).

- Evidence/snapshot scope: we ordinarily provide scoped exports (timebound logs, affected tenant objects, relevant KV cache slices). Full tenant snapshots are possible but require a signed evidence access agreement and may incur transfer/engineering fees; timing depends on retention/storage policies.

I'm attaching the internal evidence-transfer matrix and a short note from ops on what a typical 48h deliverable looks like.

Can your contracts team indicate which clauses are non-negotiable vs preferred? That will help speed the review.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence-transfer-matrix.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2025 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA discussion - incident obligations

Jordan / Ben — internal note for response drafting and redline negotiation.

Summary of constraints:
- We can operationally meet a 48-hour notification target for incidents that are detected and internally triaged. 24 hours is often feasible for confirmed exfiltration but not for initial noisy alerts; we should avoid promising 24h across the board.
- Evidence exports: provide a "standard package" within 72 hours that includes timeline, affected object list, scoped logs, and CRCs for exported files. Full tenant forensic images require a change request and an engineering window (typically 5-10 business days) plus fees.
- Subprocessor involvement: where subprocessors hold raw telemetry (e.g., CDN logs, managed backups), our obligation is to coordinate transfer; we cannot compel third-party timelines. We must add language about "reasonable commercial efforts" and a shared escalation path.

Suggested negotiation posture for Jordan:
- Offer 48-hour notification baseline.
- Offer 24-hour material-incident escalation with SLA addendum and limited credit/discount options.
- Standard evidence package within 72 hours; separate scope/pricing for full snapshots.

I'll draft specific paragraph edits for Marissa to propose.

-Kim
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: forensic-extract-instructions.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@greenfieldpay.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2025 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA discussion - incident obligations

Liam and Greenfield contracts team — thanks for the redlines and for surfacing expectations. 

We reviewed the proposed language. Key commercial/legal points below and a proposed compromise clause (summary):

1) Notification timing: Redwood will commit to notifying the customer no later than 48 hours after confirming a security incident that materially affects personal data. For "material breaches" where exfiltration of personal data is confirmed, Redwood will notify within 24 hours of confirmation.

2) Definition & confirmation: We will insert a definition for "confirmation" (e.g., validated by our SOC with corroborating telemetry) to avoid ambiguity.

3) Evidence export scope & fees: Standard evidence package (scoped logs, affected record list, timeline, export checksums) delivered within 72 hours of confirmation. Full tenant snapshots or long-range forensic exports will be provided under a signed Forensic Access Addendum; transfer and storage costs borne by the customer unless otherwise negotiated.

4) Subprocessors & cooperation: Redwood will use reasonable commercial efforts to obtain data from subprocessors and will provide a named escalation contact. If a subprocessor's timeline materially prevents timely delivery, Redwood will notify the customer and provide available interim artifacts.

5) Escrow/forensic transfer: where an escrow or third‑party transfer is requested, Redwood will coordinate the transfer and provide manifest/CRC; Redwood is not responsible for third‑party storage terms.

If these points look acceptable, we can propose the attached redline back to Greenfield. If Greenfield insists on unconditional 24-hour notification for all incidents, we'll need to route to sales leadership for an SLA exception and pricing.

Proposed next step: Liam/Contracts — confirm which of the above are must-haves vs nice-to-haves. We'll aim to send a single tracked-redline DPA by end of day Wednesday.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_redlines_response_v1.pdf

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@greenfieldpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@greenfieldpay.com, Sofia Martinez <sofia@lawfirmkhan.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA discussion - incident obligations

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary and the compromise language. That aligns with what our counsel will accept; the distinction around "confirmation" is helpful.

Two follow-ups: 
- Can you include the named subprocessor escalation contact in the redline (we need a 24/7 phone for incidents with regulatory impact)?
- For the Forensic Access Addendum, can you include a cap on engineering fees or a commitment to provide a detailed estimate within 24 hours of request?

If you can fold those in, I think we can move to signature. I'll circulate internally and get back within 24 hours.

Best,
Liam
Director, Security & Compliance
Greenfield Payments
